paper.title_en: Microwave photon scattering on superconducting bistable cells
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the problem of single microwave photon scattering in a one-dimensional waveguide coupled to one or two bistable cells, each representing a hybrid system consisting of a superconducting qubit and a nonlinear Josephson oscillator. It is shown that the initial state of the nonlinear oscillator strongly affects the resonant properties of the system, leading to a shift of the effective qubit resonance frequency and to a modification of the spectral line shape. By controlling the dynamical states of the oscillator with an external current, it becomes possible to modify the frequency dependence of the photon transmission and reflection coefficients in the waveguide. For a system containing two bistable cells, additional narrow resonant structures emerge in the resonant response spectra due to the discrete spectrum of the nonlinear oscillators. Their positions and widths are shown to depend on the phase shift between the qubits, reflecting the influence of the internal structure of the nonlinear oscillator on collective effects in the system. The obtained results demonstrate the importance of taking into account the multilevel nature of the nonlinear oscillator in the analysis of photon scattering in hybrid waveguide structures.
